provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Moving my body
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state different ways to move their bodies.
The pupils should be able to move to teacher commands.
Introduction:
We have been learning about our body parts. Today we will learn how to move them.
Content:
We can walk like we are going to the market.
We can run like a danfo bus in a hurry.
We can jump like a harmattan wind blowing.
Listen to my commands and move your body.
Class activity:
The teacher will call out commands like jump run walk and pupils will move.
Evaluation questions:
How do we move like we are going to the market?
Show me how to jump.
What do we do when the teacher says run?
Summary:
We can move our bodies in many ways like walking running and jumping.

topics.title: Marching
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to march on the spot.
The pupils should be able to march forward and back.
Introduction:
Last week we learned moving our bodies. Today we will learn marching like soldiers.
Content:
Marching means lifting your feet high and down.
We march on the spot without going anywhere.
We march forward like we are going to assembly.
We march back like we are going home.
Class activity:
The teacher will lead pupils in marching forward and back in the classroom.
Evaluation questions:
Show me how to march on the spot.
What do soldiers do when they march?
March forward three steps.
Summary:
Marching is lifting your feet high and we can march forward and back.

topics.title: Running simple races
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to run short races.
The pupils should be able to run in lanes.
Introduction:
We have learned walking and marching. Today we will learn running races.
Content:
Running is faster than walking.
A short race is like running from your house to the borehole.
We run in lanes so we do not bump into each other.
Each pupil has their own space to run.
Class activity:
The teacher will mark lanes on the ground and pupils will run short races.
Evaluation questions:
What is running?
How is running different from walking?
Show me how to run in a lane.
Summary:
We can run short races in lanes without bumping into each other.

topics.title: Jumping
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to jump on the spot.
The pupils should be able to jump over a line.
Introduction:
Last week we learned running races. Today we will learn jumping like grasshoppers.
Content:
Jumping means pushing your feet off the ground.
We can jump on the spot like we are cooking with a kerosene stove.
We can jump over a line like crossing a small stream.
Jumping makes our legs strong.
Class activity:
The teacher will draw a line on the ground and pupils will jump over it.
Evaluation questions:
Show me how to jump on the spot.
How do we jump over a line?
Why do we need strong legs for jumping?
Summary:
Jumping is pushing your feet off the ground and we can jump on the spot or over a line.

topics.title: Throwing and catching
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to throw a ball up.
The pupils should be able to catch with two hands.
Introduction:
We have learned moving our bodies. Today we will learn throwing and catching a ball.
Content:
Throwing means sending the ball up in the air.
We throw the ball up like we are selling tomatoes in the market.
Catching means stopping the ball with your hands.
We catch with two hands like holding a big bowl of rice.
Class activity:
The teacher will give each pupil a ball and they will practice throwing up and catching.
Evaluation questions:
How do we throw a ball?
Why do we use two hands to catch?
Show me how to throw and catch a ball.
Summary:
We can throw a ball up and catch it with two hands to play safely.

topics.title: Body parts exercise
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to move their arms up and down.
The pupils should be able to bend and stretch their bodies.
Introduction:
We have learned moving our whole body. Today we will exercise our body parts.
Content:
Our arms can go up like the sun rising.
Our arms can go down like the sun setting.
We can bend like a plant in the harmattan wind.
We can stretch like we are waking up from sleep.
Class activity:
The teacher will lead pupils in moving arms up and down and bending and stretching.
Evaluation questions:
Show me how to move your arms up.
How do we bend our body?
What does stretching feel like?
Summary:
We can exercise our body parts by moving arms and bending and stretching.

topics.title: Clean habits
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to wash hands after playing.
The pupils should be able to talk about clean games.
Introduction:
We have been exercising our bodies. Today we will learn about keeping clean.
Content:
We wash our hands with soap and water after playing.
Clean hands stop germs like sickness from entering our body.
We play clean games that do not make us dirty.
Clean games keep us healthy like eating good food.
Class activity:
The teacher will demonstrate washing hands and pupils will practice.
Evaluation questions:
When do we wash our hands?
Why do we need to keep our hands clean?
Name one clean game we can play.
Summary:
We wash our hands after playing and play clean games to stay healthy.

topics.title: Playing safely
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to avoid pushing on the line.
The pupils should be able to follow safe playing rules.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about clean habits. Today we will learn playing safely with friends.
Content:
We do not push when we stand in a line like buying groundnut.
Pushing can make someone fall and get hurt.
We follow rules like not running in the classroom.
Safe playing means no fighting and sharing toys.
Class activity:
The teacher will lead a game where pupils practice standing in a line without pushing.
Evaluation questions:
What should we not do in a line?
Why is pushing dangerous?
Show me how to stand safely in a line.
Summary:
We play safely by not pushing and following rules so no one gets hurt.

topics.title: Simple games: circle games
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to join a circle game.
The pupils should be able to follow circle game rules.
Introduction:
We have learned playing safely. Today we will learn playing circle games.
Content:
A circle game is when we stand in a circle and play.
We join the circle by holding hands with friends.
We follow rules like passing a ball around.
Circle games teach us to wait for our turn.
Class activity:
The teacher will lead a simple circle game where pupils pass a ball around.
Evaluation questions:
How do we join a circle game?
What rules do we follow in circle games?
Why is it important to wait for your turn?
Summary:
We can join circle games and follow rules to play happily with friends.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show skills learned this term.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term work.
Introduction:
This week we will practice all we have learned and show our skills.
Content:
We will walk run and jump to show we can move our bodies.
We will march like soldiers and play circle games.
We will talk about washing hands and playing safely.
We will answer questions about all we learned.
Class activity:
The teacher will organize a mini-sports day where pupils show different skills.
Evaluation questions:
Show me how to march.
Why do we wash our hands?
How do we play safely in a line?
What games do we play in a circle?
Summary:
We have learned many skills and we will show them to remember what we know.
